svg.title: Approvals bind the exact action
svg.desc: The registry prepares arguments, validates the descriptor schema, and freezes the canonical request. Audit capacity and effect resources are reserved before allow, ask, or deny policy is evaluated. Defaults allow read and ask for write, execute, and network. Each execution admits up to 16 interactive attempts and two simultaneous waits; silent decisions consume neither. Audit bytes admit at most 31 audited calls by default. Approved shell commands have host authority and failures do not roll back earlier effects. See docs/diagram-descriptions.md, Permissions.
svg.text: Outer tool allowance does not approve inner effects

g.text: 1. Prepare a canonical request
Resolve the action and descriptor schema.
Prepare arguments, validate, then freeze them.
Approval and invocation use the same request.
2. Reserve before asking
Calculate affected resources; reserve write intent.
Conflicting mutations are rejected before prompts.
Reserve audit capacity and provider-owned locks.
3. Apply policy to this action
ALLOW → invoke. DENY → reject without invoking.
ASK → reserve prompt quota, then request approval.
Defaults: read = allow;
write / execute / network = ask.
Interactive approval budgets
16 admitted attempts; 2 simultaneous waits.
Silent allow / deny decisions use neither counter.
Decline or cancellation still spends an attempt.
Audit budget can be tighter
64,000 bytes ÷ 2,048 per audited call → 31 calls.
The separate host-call ceiling is 64.
64 audited calls need at least 131,072 audit bytes.
Approved shell commands use host OS authority.
Failure is not rollback. Inspect effects before retry.
